subject: 5-Bullet Friday — The Craftsmanship of Robert Caro, Sexy Tunes for the Weekend, and The Mesmerizing Art of Tamara de Lempicka

bullets.title: Turn Every Page: The Adventures of Robert Caro and Robert Gottlieb
bullets.note: This is the amazing story of an iconic writer and his equally iconic (but more hilarious) editor. How do two stubborn geniuses collaborate—and productively fight—over decades? This is how. Description: “_Turn Every Page_ explores the remarkable fifty-year relationship between two literary legends, writer Robert Caro and his longtime editor Robert Gottlieb. Now 86, Caro is working to complete the final volume of his masterwork, [_The Years of Lyndon Johnson_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Years_of_Lyndon_Johnson); Gottlieb, 91, waits to edit it. The task of finishing their life’s work looms before them.” Watch the trailer [here](https://youtu.be/gv3CRojrbeE?si=Xorq7VVRMw_mET9j). Huge thanks to [Brandon Stanton](https://tim.blog/2018/06/18/brandon-stanton-humans-of-new-york/?utm_campaign=5bf&utm_medium=convertkit&utm_source=convertkit#content) of [Humans of New York](https://www.humansofnewyork.com/) for the great recommendation! This doc also covers the genesis and process story of _The Power Broker_, the masterpiece that put Caro on the literary map.

bullets.title: Tamara de Lempicka
bullets.note: I randomly found this artist’s work on the streets of NYC, and it propelled me down a rabbit hole. Her life story and art work are one-of-a-kind. Here’s a gem from [Britannica](https://www.britannica.com/biography/Tamara-de-Lempicka): “By her own account, de Lempicka sought to make a living from her art as a result of her husband’s reluctance to work.” I suppose necessity is the mother of invention! If you only have 30 seconds, [watch this video](https://youtu.be/ewFzrfamPGs). See more of her works [here](https://www.famsf.org/stories/5-things-to-know-art-deco-tamara-de-lempicka), [here](https://polandsite.proboards.com/thread/6116/tamara-empicka-art-deco), and [here](https://www.sothebys.com/en/digital-catalogues/the-world-of-tamara-a-celebration-of-lempicka-art-deco).

bullets.title: Solvitur ambulando
bullets.note: From Wikipedia: “Solvitur ambulando is a Latin phrase which means ‘it is solved by walking,’ referring to an anecdotal, practical solution to a seemingly complex philosophical problem. It is often attributed to Saint Augustine in a refutation of Zeno’s paradoxes of motion.”
